c_1709.name: calculating ionization energy
c_1709.definition: Computing the energy required to remove an electron from an atom or ion.

c_1710.name: predicting hydrogenation products
c_1710.definition: Determining the products or stereochemical outcomes of the catalytic hydrogenation of alkenes or alkynes.

c_1711.name: evaluating set paradoxes
c_1711.definition: Analyzing logical paradoxes related to set theory, such as Russell's paradox.

c_1712.name: comparing spatial coordinates
c_1712.definition: Evaluating the equality, relative position, or differences between two or more sets of spatial coordinates.
include: Checking if two points are the same
Comparing x or y values of coordinates

confusable_with.name: evaluating equality and equivalence
confusable_with.rule: Solver calculates multidimensional spatial distances, directions, or coordinate offsets between points, whereas evaluating numerical equality compares scalar values or algebraic expressions for numerical identity.

c_1713.name: evaluating demonyms
c_1713.definition: Identifying or assessing the correct demonym or nationality adjective for a given geographical location.
include: Identifying the correct term for a resident of a city

c_1714.name: applying quantum perturbation theory
c_1714.definition: Using perturbation theory to approximate the energy levels or eigenstates of a quantum system that cannot be solved exactly.

c_1715.name: evaluating lexical compatibility
c_1715.definition: Assessing whether specific words or lexical items are compatible with each other or a given context based on semantic, syntactic, or stylistic constraints.

confusable_with.name: evaluating lexical similarity
confusable_with.rule: Evaluating lexical similarity measures character-level or phonetic distances between strings (e.g., edit distance), whereas evaluating lexical compatibility analyzes semantic and syntactic fit within a given linguistic context.

c_1717.name: applying homogeneous scaling
c_1717.definition: Using the properties of homogeneous functions or scaling laws to determine how a quantity changes when its inputs are scaled.
include: Applying scaling laws to physical quantities

c_1718.name: mapping semantic similarity to options
c_1718.definition: Selecting the best candidate option by evaluating its semantic similarity to a target concept or phrase.
include: Mapping semantic similarity to multiple choice options
Matching options based on meaning overlap

c_1719.name: aggregating semantic categories
c_1719.definition: Combining or grouping multiple semantic categories or concepts into a broader, unified category.

c_1720.name: analyzing temperature dependence
c_1720.definition: Evaluating how physical or chemical properties, such as reaction rates or material characteristics, vary with changes in temperature.

c_1721.name: evaluating public health interventions
c_1721.definition: Assessing the impact, efficacy, or implementation of public health policies, interventions, or epidemiological measures.

c_1722.name: mapping conditional relations
c_1722.definition: Identifying and mapping conditional or if-then relationships between events, states, or entities.

c_1723.name: synthesizing elements
c_1723.definition: Combining multiple distinct elements, components, or pieces of information into a unified whole.

c_1724.name: determining mathematical range
c_1724.definition: Identifying the set of valid output values that a mathematical function can produce.
include: Finding the range of a function

c_1725.name: evaluating translation accuracy
c_1725.definition: Assessing whether a text is correctly and accurately translated from one language to another.
exclude: Evaluating translation accuracy of named entities
Evaluating translation accuracy of numerical values

confusable_with.name: evaluating translation accuracy of named entities
confusable_with.rule: A evaluates proper-noun translation accuracy at the span level, whereas B evaluates global semantic fidelity, fluency, and overall text accuracy across full sentences or passages.

confusable_with.name: evaluating translation accuracy of cultural references
confusable_with.rule: Skill A evaluates the pragmatic localization and cultural adaptation of specific idioms or references across languages, whereas Skill B evaluates the general semantic correctness and truth-preservation of a translated text.

c_1726.name: evaluating esterification reactions
c_1726.definition: Analyzing the reactants, products, or mechanisms of chemical reactions that form esters, typically from carboxylic acids and alcohols.

confusable_with.name: evaluating hydrolysis reactions
confusable_with.rule: Evaluating hydrolysis reactions analyzes the cleavage of a chemical bond via the addition of a water molecule, whereas evaluating esterification reactions analyzes the condensation of an alcohol and a carboxylic acid to synthesize an ester bond while eliminating water.

c_1727.name: resolving epistemic states of agents
c_1727.definition: Determining what an agent knows, believes, or perceives based on their observations and the information available to them.
